newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: AHOLD SAYS CUSTOMER COMES FIRST.
newsitem.headline: AHOLD SAYS CUSTOMER COMES FIRST.

text.p: The customer is king as far as Dutch supermarket giant Ahold NV is concerned, coming ahead of staff and shareholders, chairman Cees van der Hoeven said in an interview on Tuesday.
"If we want to set our priorities...the customer is number one," Van der Hoeven said, adding that second priority would be given to employees.
"The way we work, our employees are number two," he said.
Van der Hoeven said shareholders would benefit automatically from Ahold taking good care of its first two priorities.
"One is a consequence of the other," he said.

"We don't (necessarily) aim (to please shareholders with good) quarterly figures. We target long-term shareholder value, but realise that by giving priority to the customer and by creating such a working climate our employees are very motivated.
"That way, the shareholder gets what he wants," he said.
Van der Hoeven said Ahold set clear goals for shareholders.
"Since 1992, we've always said we aimed to double our profit within five years...we have more than succeeded."
"The next step is...to reach at least 15 percent annual growth in profits per share...," Van der Hoeven said.
Last week Ahold posted 39 percent higher 1996 net of 632.4 million guilders, boosting earnings per share by 16.7 percent.
It expects earnings per share to grow significantly in 1997.
